entry_point.discipline_context: Parameter fitting and design tuning in mechanical engineering use a scalar performance objective over a vector of design variables.
entry_point.rationale: Learners can connect familiar gradients and matrix curvature to a systematic optimisation workflow before meeting formal convexity.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: Engineering language motivates the examples; the definitions, algorithms, assumptions, and rates below are mathematical statements.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: Exact line search is requested and provides a direct comparison with adaptive step selection.
Armijo backtracking is requested as a practical step-size strategy.
Heavy Ball is explicitly requested for comparison with gradient descent.
The requested acceleration scope includes the approved quadratic Heavy Ball result.
The requested acceleration scope includes the Nesterov convergence result.
The requested stochastic-gradient scope includes its update and error-floor qualification.
Step-size conditions for stochastic gradients are explicitly requested.
Newton's second-order model is explicitly requested.
Newton's implementation update is explicitly requested.
The requested Newton scope includes its local convergence result.
The requested BFGS scope includes its curvature condition and direction.

chapter_sequence.title: From engineering design to an optimisation problem
chapter_sequence.purpose: Define unconstrained optimisation, stationarity, and first- and second-order tests.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and the geometry of curvature
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build the assumptions behind global lower bounds, quadratic upper bounds, Hessian tests, and condition numbers.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and choosing a step
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain the basic update, fixed steps, exact line search, Armijo backtracking, and convergence rates.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum, acceleration, and stochastic gradients
chapter_sequence.purpose: Compare Heavy Ball and the specified Nesterov recurrence, then introduce stochastic assumptions and diminishing steps.

chapter_sequence.title: Coordinate scaling and adaptive methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam as distinct moment or accumulation updates.

chapter_sequence.title: Using curvature: Newton and BFGS
chapter_sequence.purpose: Connect Taylor models, linear solves, local Newton convergence, and the BFGS secant update to implementation.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Consolidate theorem scope, one gradient update, and Python implementation diagnosis.

implementation_strategy: Show each mathematical update beside a short executable Python pattern, emphasising current versus look-ahead gradients, element-wise operations, bias correction, and linear solves.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly three final worked exercises: a theorem-scope check, a unified objective-gradient-update calculation, and a code diagnostic with buggy and corrected code.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Distinguish the hypotheses and conclusions of convex GD, strongly convex GD, Heavy Ball, NAG, and Newton results.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Choose a trustworthy solver for a parameter-identification objective in a compliant finite-element model.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Differentiate a quadratic objective and perform one positive-step gradient descent update.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Update two design variables in a simple quadratic calibration objective.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Identify a sign and evaluation-point error in gradient descent code and verify the corrected update.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Inspect a small optimisation routine used to tune a pair of stiffness-related parameters.
